attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised claim matches the sentence. It is a present-tense claim about the technical position of Sora and similar generative systems. It is not hedged. 'No way to encode (and guarantee)' is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: Sora-like general-purpose systems, broad real-world constraints, and the state of the art at the time of the post. It correctly separates a narrow formal constraint from a general guarantee, and lacking a guarantee from impossibility. The result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure, dated 2024-02-15, shows Sora's physics failures. Failures in outputs do not prove that no enforcement method existed.
Pre-post theoretical paper on LLM hallucination in a formal world. Its scope is LLM text, so it does not settle physics or object continuity for Sora.
Hard mass-conservation constraint in a specialised turbulence GAN. Under the contract this narrow constraint is not a counterexample for a general-purpose system.
Shows calibrated LMs must hallucinate arbitrary facts but other errors may be mitigated. It offers no general guarantee and no proof of impossibility for Sora.

reviews.rationale: No item shows a method available by February 2024 that guaranteed truthfulness, physics, or object permanence in a general-purpose generator, so the claim is not contradicted. Nor does any item show such enforcement was unavailable across the system class. Sora's failures and the LLM theory papers are context only. The packet does not settle the claim.
